si.t: Multi-role e-commerce system (Buyer, Seller, Logistics, Rider)
1. Read the Assumptions sheet first. The rules are modeled on Philippine marketplaces, so adjust any case whose rule differs from your system.
2. The Test Data sheet lists every form field with two ready-made accounts per role. The Test Files sheet lists the upload files to prepare. All people, companies and numbers are fictional.
3. Emails use example.com, so nothing is delivered to a real inbox. Read OTP and activation emails from a mail catcher such as Mailtrap, or from your application's mail log.

4. On each role sheet, run the Test Steps with the Test Data and compare what happens with the Expected Result. Use a spare email and mobile number from the Test Data sheet whenever a value marked (accept) creates another account.
5. Dates of birth and license expiry dates in the boundary cases are calculated from today's date, so they are always correct on the day you test.
6. Fill in only the yellow cells: Actual Result, Status and Remarks. Pick the Status from the dropdown (Pass, Fail, Blocked, Not Run).

7. Pass = actual matches expected. Fail = it does not (describe what happened and add a screenshot or bug number in Remarks). Blocked = the case could not be run, for example because an earlier case failed.
8. The Results by role table above updates automatically from the Status column.

Inputs are grouped into valid and invalid classes, and one value from each class is tested.
Values at and just beyond a limit are tested, for example 7 and 8 characters for a minimum of 8.
Combinations of conditions are tested, for example each missing password character type.
Changes in account status are tested, for example Unverified to Active or Pending Approval to Approved.
A complete user flow is tested from start to finish with valid data.
Likely mistakes are tested based on experience, for example double-clicking Register or pasting another role's URL.

Assumptions used in the test cases

These rules are modeled on Philippine marketplaces, not taken from your actual system. Write your real rule in column D where it differs, then filter the Assumption Ref column on each role sheet to find the test cases to adjust.
Your system's actual rule (fill in if different)
Each role's form has the fields listed on the Test Data sheet, modeled on Philippine marketplaces. Payout details (bank or e-wallet) are set up after approval, not during registration.
2 to 50 characters. Letters (including ñ), spaces, hyphen, apostrophe and period only.
Must be a valid email format. Unique across all roles (one email = one account). Not case-sensitive. Leading and trailing spaces are removed.
Philippine mobile number entered as 09XXXXXXXXX (11 digits) or +639XXXXXXXXX. Both forms are stored as the same number. Unique across all accounts.
At least 8 characters with at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number and one special character. Confirm Password must match.
Buyers and riders must be at least 18 years old on the day of registration. A future date is not allowed.
Region, Province, City/Municipality and Barangay are linked dropdowns: each list depends on the one before it. Postal Code is exactly 4 digits.
12 digits in the form 000-000-000-000 (9-digit TIN plus 3-digit branch code). Unique across seller and logistics accounts.
A 6-digit numeric code is emailed after registration. It is valid for 5 minutes. Resending creates a new code and cancels the old one. An account cannot be used until it is verified.
Accepted file types: JPG, PNG, PDF. Maximum size: 5 MB (5,120 KB) per file.

Individual: Government-issued ID. Sole Proprietorship: Government-issued ID, DTI Certificate and BIR Form 2303. Corporation: Government-issued ID of the representative, SEC Certificate and BIR Form 2303.

Buyer: Unverified, then Active after OTP. Seller and Logistics: Unverified, then Pending Approval after OTP, then Approved or Rejected by an admin. A rejected applicant can correct the details and resubmit.

Riders cannot register themselves. Only an Approved logistics account can create a rider. The rider starts as Pending Activation and becomes Active after setting a password through an emailed activation link, which is valid for 24 hours. Riders do not need separate admin approval.
Shop Name (3 to 30 characters), Company Name, SEC Registration No. (2 letters followed by 9 digits), Driver's License No. and Plate Number must each be unique.
License number follows the LTO form A00-00-000000 (1 letter and 11 digits). The expiry date must be today or a later date.
